goal.title: Build all-skills configuration and production assurance
goal.outcome: Provide one suite-wide versioned JSON configuration boundary for all 14 skills with incremental adapters, then make csm-orchestrate production-grade through SQLite WAL durability, host assurance, independent validation, telemetry, evaluation, rollout, and rollback gates.
constraints: Configuration precedence is built-in defaults -> project -> user -> one per-run override.
User configuration is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/csm/skills.json, falling back to ~/.config/csm/skills.json.
A per-run override is one explicit local configPath/--config path.
Objects merge recursively, arrays replace wholesale, null is explicit, and unknown keys/revisions fail.
${VAR_NAME} references are one-pass string substitutions; any variable name is permitted by explicit user decision and resolved values may be persisted.
No-config behavior and direct skill APIs remain compatible.
Each skill owns its namespace schema, native defaults, lifecycle, artifacts, and semantic adapter.
SQLite WAL is the initial local coordination authority; external effects are at-least-once with reconciliation and sink idempotency where available.
Production autonomy remains disabled until every production gate has observed evidence.
exclusions: Do not create a universal semantic policy object across skills.
Do not let configuration grant capabilities, credentials, trust roots, lifecycle transitions, evaluator authority, publication authority, or hard safety ceilings.
Do not claim exactly-once arbitrary external effects.
Do not silently migrate or rewrite legacy csm-upload configuration.
Do not replace sibling lifecycles or producer artifact ownership.
Do not enable production autonomy based on green CI or synthetic fixtures alone.

observations: The agreed approach defines eight phases from contract freeze through controlled autonomy.
The final research concludes that a common configuration transport layer is viable but a universal semantic policy merge is unsafe across 14 skills.

The repository has schema registry, compatibility matrix, artifact resolver, durable-json, bootstrap packer, and csm-orchestrate receipt/cursor seams, but no suite config loader or SQLite coordination adapter.

csm-orchestrate currently exposes host/cursor/review seams but does not provide production host authentication, cross-process CAS/fencing/history, semantic signal validators, or rollout infrastructure.
The working tree is clean at baseline; implementation must preserve the unrelated process-artifact history already committed.

design.configEnvelope: csm-skills-config/1 with closed schema, version, skills namespaces, source records, per-skill schema references, effective snapshot, precedence record, environment-reference record, and effective digest.
design.configMerge: Parse each source independently; expand ${VAR_NAME} once in strings; recursively merge objects; replace arrays; preserve explicit null; validate the final effective namespaces and semantic adapter constraints; reject unknown keys, duplicate keys, invalid revisions, missing variables, malformed explicit files, and unsupported values.
design.ownership: Shared runtime owns loading, parsing, merge, provenance, digest, and compatibility transport. Each skill owns its namespace schema, defaults, semantic validation, lifecycle, and artifacts. Host owns authority, ceilings, credentials, isolation, durable coordination, approval authenticity, final sinks, and external effects.
design.orchestration: Canonical request/config/input/graph/policy digests feed exact one-time approvals, fenced dispatch intents, independent validator/reviewer attestations, durable SQLite history, monotonic receipts, telemetry, and reconciliation. Timeout/cancel uncertainty is UNKNOWN.
design.sqlite: SQLite WAL on a local non-network filesystem; tables for schema version, run/phase/node/attempt, cursor CAS, leases/fencing, approvals, idempotency, dispatch intents, events, terminal receipts, late results, cancellation, remediation budget, and graph revisions. Use transactions and unique constraints; keep filesystem artifacts as resolver-validated projections.

risks: A suite-wide config file creates a broad malformed-input blast radius.
Project/user/per-run settings can be mistaken for authority or widen behavior if adapters are permissive.
Persisting arbitrary environment values may expose secrets despite the user decision.
SQLite coordinates local metadata but cannot atomically control arbitrary external effects.
Timeout/cancellation can leave unknown side effects and late completions.
Schema adapters can preserve shape while changing security semantics.
Synthetic reviewers, validators, and canaries can create false production confidence.
Bootstrap and source registries can drift if generated artifacts are hand-edited.

Require sink reconciliation or idempotency before retrying effectful work.
Version schemas explicitly, test semantic adapters, and bind all records to effective digests.

risksAndRecovery.rollback: Each adapter/config/schema release is versioned and can be disabled by active-version pointer. Rollback stops new dispatch, fences the bad version, preserves receipts/history, and reconciles in-flight effects; it never deletes prior evidence.
risksAndRecovery.forwardRecovery: If a task fails, retain its checkpoint and artifacts, add a bounded repair task, rerun the affected acceptance signal plus downstream gates, and do not widen scope or silently downgrade a production requirement.
